People work together in a shared space.
Pexels · 6913336
Working together
There is more than one way to finish a task together. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others
are two useful starting points.
One reason is that clear responsibilities help people know what to do. For instance, we agree who will prepare the
notes and who will check the figures. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves
us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that asking for help early prevents a small problem from becoming a large one. For example, we
discuss an unclear instruction before spending an hour on the wrong task. This approach recognises that the
experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail.
We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Review without reading the example first. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two
reasons are that clear responsibilities help people know what to do and that asking for help early prevents a small problem
from becoming a large one. One example is that we agree who will prepare the notes and who will check the figures.)
